content.content: 1 # configurable-tree-traversal 2 3 **Dependency-aware building blocks for autonomous-agent workflows, plus general graph and tree traversal for TypeScript and JavaScript.** 4 5 Give CTT a graph of work and accepted completion facts. It determines what can run next, enforces work and structural-completion dependencies, and exposes progress without executing business work. Your host chooses agents, dispatches tasks, accepts results, and persists state. 6 7 [Documentation map](docs/index.md) · [Agent workflow guide](docs/agent-workflows.md) · [API reference](docs/reference.md) · [Client API migration](docs/migration-client-api.md) · [Idiomatic API migration](docs/migration-idiomatic-api.md) · [API naming migration](docs/migration-api-clarity.md) · [Uniform API migration](docs/migration-uniform-api.md) · [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/configurable-tree-traversal) 8 9 ## Start with autonomous agents 10 11 | You want to… | Use CTT for… | Start here | 12 | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 13 | Coordinate research, implementation, testing, and review agents | Parallel branches and dependency joins | [Quickstart](#quickstart-find-the-next-agent-tasks) | 14 | Let a coordinator choose which agents run next | Deferred work and generation-bearing dispatch records | [Host-controlled execution](docs/agent-workflows.md#choose-an-execution-model) | 15 | Resume after a process restart or wait for human input | Reconstruction from accepted completion facts | [Recovery and storage](docs/agent-workflows.md#persist-facts-and-reconstruct) | 16 | Review a composite task only after all its subtasks finish | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion` | [Work versus completion](docs/agent-workflows.md#work-dependencies-and-completion-joins) | 17 | Fetch dependencies from a task catalog or service | `resolvePrerequisite(id)` | [Discover prerequisites](docs/agent-workflows.md#discover-the-graph) | 18 | Explore cyclic context, code references, or provenance | Lazy typed vertex/edge/path walking with explicit bounds | [Graph exploration](docs/agent-workflows.md#explore-context-and-references) | 19 | Walk or transform a repository index, AST, or JSON object | Iterative sync/async DFS, BFS, pruning, rewriting | [Tree and object traversal](docs/reference.md#traverse-an-object) | 20 21 CTT is an in-memory traversal engine. The host owns workflow meaning, agent/tool execution, claims, retries, timeouts, business outcomes, and durable storage. It can use SQLite, another database, or another storage provider without a CTT storage dependency. 22 23 ## Install 24 25 ```sh 26 npm install configurable-tree-traversal 27 ``` 28 29 Requires Node **22.12.0+**, or Bun **1.4.4**. CI covers the minimum Node runtime, current Node 22/24, and Bun. TypeScript consumers are checked with 4.7.4 and 4.9.5. 30 31 ## Quickstart: find the next agent tasks 32 33 After `research` completes, `implement` and `testPlan` can run independently. `review` waits for both. Supply a flat task collection with explicit work dependencies: 34 35 ```text 36 research ──┬── implement ──┬── review 37 └── testPlan ───┘ 38 ``` 39 40 41 42 ```ts 43 import { 44 materializeDagInputFromRecords, 45 prepareDag, 46 } from 'configurable-tree-traversal'; 47 48 const tasks = [ 49 { id: 'research', requires: [] }, 50 { id: 'implement', requires: ['research'] }, 51 { id: 'testPlan', requires: ['research'] }, 52 { id: 'review', requires: ['implement', 'testPlan'] }, 53 ]; 54 const prepared = prepareDag( 55 materializeDagInputFromRecords(tasks, { 56 id: (task) => task.id, 57 dependsOnWork: (task) => task.requires, 58 }), 59 ); 60 if (prepared.kind === 'invalid') 61 throw new Error('Invalid dependency constraints'); 62 63 // In-memory stand-in for completion facts already accepted by the host. 64 const accepted = new Set(['research']); 65 const session = prepared.dag.createWorkSession({ completedWork: accepted }); 66 const boundary = session.advance(); 67 if (boundary.kind === 'awaitingSettlement') { 68 if ( 69 boundary.workTickets.map((ticket) => ticket.vertexId).join(',') !== 70 'implement,testPlan' 71 ) { 72 throw new Error('Unexpected ready tasks'); 73 } 74 // Retain each frontier ticket with its host attempt. 75 const ticket = boundary.workTickets[0]!; 76 // Dispatch through host claims/capacity, then validate and persist the result. 77 accepted.add(ticket.vertexId); // Simulate durable acceptance. 78 session.completeWork(ticket); // { kind: 'accepted' } 79 const next = session.advance(); // Observe newly eligible work. 80 if (next.kind !== 'awaitingSettlement') 81 throw new Error('Expected pending work'); 82 } 83 ``` 84 85 `materializeDagInputFromRecords` returns a `MaterializedDagInput` envelope (`traversableGraph` plus `syntheticRoot: true`) and copies collection membership and edge lists while sharing task data. `prepareDag` eagerly discovers and validates without executing work. Dependency validation failures and engine-discovered structural cycles return `invalid`; exact source failures and malformed inputs throw (see [preparation errors](docs/reference.md#reusable-prepared-dags)). Its reusable definition creates independent sessions without repeating source I/O. A session uses external settlement: `advance()` returns work tickets, `paused`, or `finished`; `completeWork(ticket)` accepts work without dispatching agents. Dispatch from `advance().workTickets` tickets; `ON_WORK_READY` visitors can also start work before deferral. `workCompleted` iterator events report work **after** commitment, so they are observations, not dispatch requests. Tickets belong to the issuing session and stay local. The host owns claims, durable acceptance, retries, and recovery from accepted facts. Build reusable workflow shapes with [typed fragments and explicit W/C composition](docs/reference.md#dag-fragments-and-composition). 86 87 See the [workflow guide](docs/agent-workflows.md#accept-results-and-resume) and [executable example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/agent-api-foundations-example.ts) for independent sessions, duplicate reports, and recovery. Custom graph adapters and existing `runner.prepare()` / guarded `settle()` APIs remain available. 88 89 ## Choose your next page 90 91 - **Integrating an agent coordinator:** [Agent workflows](docs/agent-workflows.md), including execution models, persistence, retries, and common mistakes. 92 - **Looking up a contract:** [API and behavior reference](docs/reference.md), including tree traversal, commands, identity, errors, and async semantics. 93 - **Finding runnable code or source:** [Documentation index](docs/index.md). 94 - **Changing CTT:** [Repository agent guide](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [testing guide](docs/testing.md). 95 - **Checking releases:** [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md). 96 97 ## Imports and compatibility 98 99 100 101 ```ts 102 import { 103 DagTraversal, 104 TraversalVisitorCommandName, 105 } from 'configurable-tree-traversal'; 106 ``` 107 108 ```js 109 const { 110 DagTraversal, 111 TraversalVisitorCommandName, 112 } = require('configurable-tree-traversal'); 113 ``` 114 115 Native ESM `.mjs` entries and `.d.mts` declarations share one CommonJS implementation and canonical types. Named/default imports, classes, namespaces, and commands preserve identity across loaders. ESM entries use Node-compatible `createRequire`; standalone browser ESM and tree shaking are not promised. Nine explicit runtime entry points are supported; historical deep imports are blocked; see [compatibility details](docs/reference.md#api-compatibility). 116 117 ## Reference shortcuts 118 119 Existing README section links land here; each topic now has a dedicated location in the reference. 120 121 | Topic | Detailed guidance | 122 | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 123 | DAG traversal | [Read section](docs/reference.md#dag-traversal) | 124 | Discovery and execution as separate phases | [Read section](docs/reference.md#discovery-and-execution-as-separate-phases) | 125 | Discovery and completed work | [Read section](docs/reference.md#discovery-and-completed-work) | 126 | Deferred DAG progress and reconciliation | [Read section](docs/reference.md#deferred-dag-progress-and-reconciliation) | 127 | Host policy and traversal feedback | [Read section](docs/reference.md#host-policy-and-traversal-feedback) | 128 | Traverse an object | [Read section](docs/reference.md#traverse-an-object) | 129 | Abstract trees | [Read section](docs/reference.md#abstract-trees) | 130 | Traversal orders | [Read section](docs/reference.md#traversal-orders) | 131 | Breadth-first traversal | [Read section](docs/reference.md#breadth-first-traversal) | 132 | Async traversal | [Read section](docs/reference.md#async-traversal) | 133 | Visitors and commands | [Read section](docs/reference.md#visitors-and-commands) | 134 | Pause and resume | [Read section](docs/reference.md#pause-and-resume) | 135 | Inspection and execution | [Read section](docs/reference.md#inspection-and-execution) | 136 | Rewrite objects | [Read section](docs/reference.md#rewrite-objects) | 137 | API compatibility | [Read section](docs/reference.md#api-compatibility) | 138 | Development | [Read section](docs/reference.md#development) | 139 140 MIT licensed. 141 142 For the breaking naming, ownership and output-presence changes, see the [client API distinctions migration](docs/migration-api-distinctions.md). 143

The [client API migration](docs/migration-client-api.md) covers the twenty client contract corrections. The [idiomatic API migration](docs/migration-idiomatic-api.md) covers the canonical removal checklist and corrected object contracts. The [migration guide](docs/migration-uniform-api.md) covers changed defaults and removed compatibility forms. `docs/research/` and `docs/superpowers/` contain historical research, plans, and downstream proposals. They are not a substitute for current documentation or evidence that a proposed feature exists. Reconcile discrepancies against source and behavioral tests; update the current guide when changing behavior.

11	## Scope and boundaries
12	
13	CTT owns generic tree/graph discovery, work/completion dependencies, callback scheduling, traversal lifecycle, diagnostics, and in-memory progress. Keep task types, agent dispatch, business priority/outcomes, attempts/retries, claims, artifact policy, and durable storage in the host. `$data` is opaque caller data; `$childHints` contains opaque discovery hints. `$d`/`$c` inputs and accessors are removed; Vertex fields and serialization use `$data`/`$childHints`. There is no public `planDag`, storage-provider port, durable runner checkpoint, or built-in LLM integration.
14	
15	Dependency edges and structural child edges are different. Under default `afterWorkReadyChain`, normal `ON_WORK_READY` completion satisfies W; committed `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` satisfies C. Use `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'` for host-controlled work, including zero/filtered callbacks; prepare a fresh runner for an eager validated preview, then run and dispatch from `summary().awaitingSettlement` records with atomic generation guards. Preparation freezes topology; run adopts discovery without replay. Dispatch from `advance().workTickets` or enabled pre-work visitors. DAG event kinds `workCompleted`/`subgraphCompleted` are committed W/C observations; callback-before-commit and event-after-commit timing remain. Deferred `workCompleted` events emit on settlement; seeds synthesize no work event. Explicit sole `DEFER_WORK_COMPLETION` ends a chain early; `PAUSE_TRAVERSAL` pauses it. `getStopReason()` distinguishes pause from awaiting settlement. Graph sources default to `rootWorkDependencies: 'honor'` and `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'none'`; express execution dependencies explicitly. Explicit graph dependency policies reject on TreeSource inputs; tree order is preserved. Deletion commands follow the runner family: `DELETE_TREE_SUBTREE` or `DELETE_DAG_VERTEX_CASCADE`. Stored-tree deletion is `deleteSubtree`, revision removal is `removeVertexDeclaration`, and multi-entry definitions use ordered `roots` slots. `SKIP_REMAINING_CHILDREN` skips pending local expansion; `SET_VISITOR_CHAIN_STATE` accepts `{ state }` for the current phase chain. Source callbacks use tagged `found`/`omitted` results; only prerequisite lookup accepts `missing`. `emitEvents` and `visitorPhases` select events/callbacks independently and patch field-wise. Flat visitors sort by priority before batching; explicit ordered groups own their batching policy. `commandCommitMode` is independent of async concurrency. Tree sources forbid graph metadata. Prefer `resolveChildHook`, typed object patches, `getResolvedTreeView()`, `getRefId()` and graph `requireVertexId`/`getVertexRefById`; ordinary tree/DAG observations expose canonical VertexHandle/VertexView facets, frozen detached hint/topology collections, and shallow caller payload identity. Tree contexts use resolvedTreeView; graph contexts use resolvedGraphView/getResolvedGraphView. Ordinary runners expose no live mutable store or independent traversal-root predicate. Synthetic entry source parents have both parent fields null; tree parents stay non-null. Use family-safe execution capabilities and cooperative `requestPause`; requests drain admitted callbacks without cancellation before acknowledgement. Rewrite output uses present/absent tagged results and defaults to unknown; `rewriteObjectAs` asserts output and `getOutputResult()` requires FINISHED. The rewrite helper owns its source. Visitor registration queries return detached records with shared callbacks/group metadata. Graph ID generics trail T/R (visitor ID follows phase); typed live results require own IDs and public views hide synthetic holders. Runner constructors, raw containers/state, normalized options and deep engine paths are private; use public factories, capability interfaces and the explicit supported entry points. Diagnostic edges are original milestone constraints, waiter waits for prerequisite; structural cycle componentVertexIds are SCC membership; discovery cycleWitnessVertexIds are ordered closed witnesses. Settlement generations are local symbols; reconstruction uses host-accepted `completedWork` facts. `inspectDagMilestones` captures observational milestone snapshots. Inspection uses ready/chain `phase`, chain `state`/`visitorIndex`/`executionOptions`, and request `operation`; graph `visitStage`/`getVisitStageOf` describes scheduling boundaries, separately from callback counts, DAG W/C, and runner lifecycle status. `PreparedDag.liveVertexSummaries` is a live-child convenience projection; `PreparedDag.definition` preserves ordered slots/omissions; mapDagFragmentIds maps fragment IDs explicitly and compose structural links separately from W/C wires. `reviseDag` validates an ordered batch against a private candidate and returns a fresh prepared DAG plus a shallow diff; old sessions, tickets and admitted callbacks remain local and no completion facts migrate.
16	
17	`MaterializedDagInput` and `materializeDagInputFromRecords`/`materializeDagInputFromRoots` (plus Async counterparts) return `{ traversableGraph, syntheticRoot: true }` envelopes. Pass or spread the entire input; `DagDiscoverySource` is the actual protocol. Walking materializers return actual `GraphWalkSource` protocols and retain source names.
18	
19	Walking uses `GraphWalk`/`AsyncGraphWalk` sources with explicit target wrappers; it does not consume arbitrary tree/DAG sources directly. Revisit, callbacks and emission are independent. First admitted resolution (including omission) wins; rejected links do not seed cache. Default once preserves parallel/back edges; bounded route modes report summary outcomes. All family selectors filter at delivery, including buffered records and deferred settlement events; callback admission snapshots stay independent. Chain inspection emitEvents is historical, while top-level executionOptions governs delivery. Callbacks are serial; own concurrency options reject. Consumer iterator return pauses; terminal runner close disposes open source iterators in reverse acquisition order. Closing FAILED rethrows the exact retained error without repeated cleanup; overlapping async closes share a promise. Configure replaceLimits records replace prior limits records and merged validation is atomic. `GraphWalkDagRelation` labels are adapter-owned/detached; caller edge data retains identity. General execution capabilities default to `ExecutionInspection` and `EmissionKind<Phase>`, preserving family phases. Concrete tree/DAG runners use `TreeDagExecutionInspection`; walkers use `GraphWalkInspection`. Tree callbacks use `TreeVisitor`/`AsyncTreeVisitor`, with structural source protocols and no empty runtime bases.

## Commands and validation

```sh
npm ci
npm run check
npm test -- tests/dag-prerequisite-resolution.test.ts
npm run tsfile -- examples/agent-orchestration-example.ts
npm run verify-examples
npm run verify-package
```

`npm run check` covers typechecking, lint, all source tests with 100% coverage, examples, build, packed runtime/type consumers, and benchmark/generator checks. For behavior changes, reproduce the issue with a focused public regression, then run the full check. For documentation changes, execute new/changed examples, verify relative links/anchors and packaged guides, and use the standard check before integration. Do not weaken coverage to pass.

The async runtime shares a state-machine core with sync runners; test affected sync/async and tree/graph families when changing shared behavior; include walking when changing common capabilities/selectors/registration. Preserve arbitrary ID identity and exact error values. ESM and CJS must share constructors, sentinels, namespaces, and declaration identity; verify packed consumers, not just source imports.

## Documentation upkeep

Keep README concise and autonomous-agent use cases first. Put integration decisions in `docs/agent-workflows.md`, detailed contracts in `docs/reference.md`, and navigation in `docs/index.md`. Keep runnable examples under `examples/`; the example verifier discovers every top-level `.ts` file. Update package `files` entries when adding a consumer guide so npm readers can follow relative links. Link repository-only examples/history through GitHub from packaged docs. Preserve existing public section anchors when moving content.

Do not infer publication authorization from test/build commands. Release and external-write actions follow the user's current instructions. Preserve unrelated local changes and never include credentials in examples or logs.

| Debug missing work or a stalled graph            | [Troubleshooting](agent-workflows.md#troubleshoot-a-workflow) → [DAG diagnostics](reference.md#dag-traversal)                                                                                                                              | A complete catalog or lookup adapter and the relevant diagnostics                                                                              |

1	# Autonomous-agent workflows with CTT
2	
3	[Documentation map](index.md) · [Quickstart](../README.md#quickstart-find-the-next-agent-tasks) · [API reference](reference.md)
4	
5	Use CTT when agents or tools perform work with dependencies: research before implementation, independent specialist tasks in parallel, verification after several branches, or review after an entire composite completes. CTT supplies graph discovery, dependency readiness, lifecycle transitions, and inspection. Your coordinator supplies the workflow and executes it.
6	
7	## On this page
8	
9	- [Explore context and references](#explore-context-and-references)
10	- [Reuse workflow fragments](#reuse-workflow-fragments)
11	- [Choose an execution model](#choose-an-execution-model)
12	- [Discover the graph](#discover-the-graph)
13	- [Work dependencies and completion joins](#work-dependencies-and-completion-joins)
14	- [Accept results and resume](#accept-results-and-resume)
15	- [Persist facts and reconstruct](#persist-facts-and-reconstruct)
16	- [Retries, human waits, and graph revisions](#retries-human-waits-and-graph-revisions)
17	- [Troubleshoot a workflow](#troubleshoot-a-workflow)
18	
19	## Explore context and references
20	
21	Choose `GraphWalk` / `AsyncGraphWalk` to gather context, follow code references or collect provenance from cyclic/shared information graphs. Choose DAG traversal when relationships mean work/completion prerequisites. A walking edge has caller-defined meaning and supplies no dispatch readiness. A found isolated root still produces a vertex; parallel and back edges remain observable in the same walk. See the [five-vertex/six-relationship context example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-context-example.ts) and [exact walking contracts](reference.md#general-graph-walking).
22	
23	For a finite in-memory catalog, use `materializeWalkSourceFromRecords(items, { id, outgoing, roots })`; its async counterpart materializes async inputs once and returns a synchronous source. For lazy retrieval, supply `source.roots()` and `source.outgoing(vertex)` with an explicit hydration mode. Use `hydration: 'resolver'` with required `resolveVertex(id)` and mixed `{ vertexId }` / `{ vertexId, resolution }` targets. Use `hydration: 'inlineOrCached'` without a resolver and tagged `{ kind: 'inline', vertexId, resolution }` / `{ kind: 'cached', vertexId }` targets; cached targets require a prior admitted resolution, including for self/backedges. Walking materializers declare resolver mode. Reuse `GraphWalkRecordSelectors` / `AsyncGraphWalkRecordSelectors` for catalogs; `GraphWalkCatalogLink` has readonly `to`/`data` fields, separate from lazy target wrappers. `materializeWalkSourceFromDagDefinition(definition, { relations })` explicitly projects selected declaration links without DAG execution validation. Do not pass a `DagDiscoverySource` / `TreeSource` directly; their source context and omission contracts differ.
24	
25	Use phase-keyed vertex and edge visitors to collect typed endpoint data in one session. Use `iterateEvents({ emitEvents: [...] })` for pull integration; explicit selections narrow the delivered event union, while callbacks are independently controlled by `visitorPhases`. `walkGraph(options)` / `await walkGraphAsync(options)` are one-shot helpers returning the runner. Source callbacks and visitors execute serially, including async walking; no concurrency setting is accepted. The [reference example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-references-example.ts) shows callbacks, async iteration, endpoint discriminants, common inspection and wrappers that preserve each family's phase type.
26	
27	Default `revisit: 'once'` collects each vertex and every followed relationship. Select `simplePaths` for prefixes without repeated vertices, or `walks` for repeated routes; both require a depth or candidate-read-attempt bound. Always carry `runner.summary().outcome` into a host result so `limited` cannot be mistaken for completeness. Paths include every prefix; parallel relationships can produce identical vertex sequences with distinct edge indices. DFS depth bounds apply to its first route; BFS finds shortest discovery depths. See the [bounded provenance example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-paths-example.ts).
28	
29	The host owns authorization, retrieval policy, stable IDs, relationship meaning, retries, freshness, timeouts, persistence and any agent/model invocation. The first admitted resolution for an ID wins, including omission; a fresh runner is required to observe replacement data. Walking does not retry omissions or certify a remote transactional snapshot. A budget bounds candidate read attempts, admitted targets and depth, not host callback duration or tokens. Consumer iterator `return()`/loop break pauses and retains resources for continuation; terminal runner `close()` disposes them after execution ownership has been released. Active terminal close rejects: first return the iterator or request and await pause. Iterator return/pause and async cleanup require pending host work to settle and do not cancel promises. A failed runner retains its exact error; closing it rethrows that same error without repeating cleanup. Retain/dispose paused runners deliberately; there is no durable walking checkpoint or built-in network/LLM integration.
30	
31	## Reuse workflow fragments
32	
33	Capture a discovered topology through `prepared.definition`, or author materialized source facts with `defineDag` and validate them with `prepareDagDefinition`. `defineDagFragment(definition, ports)` names live local boundary vertices. Keep each fragment closed over its live and known omitted identities; provide all cross-fragment dependencies when composing.
34	
35	Instantiate a template with `mapDagFragmentIds(fragment, { mapId })`, giving each local identity a host-selected global ID. Mapping runs once per live/omitted identity and supports object IDs. Then `composeDag(instances, { dependencies, children })` concatenates ordered entries and validates the entire graph. Choose `milestone: 'work'` to wait for accepted initial work or `'subgraphCompletion'` to wait for the full retained subgraph. Structural child links and execution waits are separate options.
36	
37	Invalid ports, identity collisions and nonexistent wire endpoints throw `TypeError`; cycles between valid endpoints return invalid issues. Only a valid result exposes a prepared DAG. Create independent runners or sessions from that result, selecting accepted completion facts explicitly for each run. Templates, agent roles, claims and business outcomes remain host data and policy. See the [fragment contract](reference.md#dag-fragments-and-composition) and [runnable example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-fragments-example.ts).
38	
39	## Choose an execution model
40	
41	| Model                    | How it works                                                                                                                                                                | Appropriate when                                                                      |
42	| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
43	| Host-controlled frontier | Use a prepared DAG's `createWorkSession()`, then `advance()` and dispatch its frontier tickets; custom runners can use `bindDagWorkSession` / `bindAsyncDagWorkSession` | Agents run externally, work needs claims/approval, or state must survive process loss |
44	| Work inside visitors     | Use `AsyncDagTraversal` and await work in `ON_WORK_READY` visitors; normal chain completion releases dependents                                                             | One process owns execution and immediate callback failure should fail traversal       |
45	
46	Start with the host-controlled model for a durable agent coordinator. For in-memory collections, use `materializeDagInputFromRecords` → `prepareDag` → `dag.createWorkSession({ completedWork })`. Use `await prepareDagAsync(...)` for async source discovery and `await dag.createAsyncWorkSession(...)` for an async session. `DagTraversal` is sufficient when graph facts are already in memory; use `AsyncDagTraversal` for asynchronous adapters. The host can run asynchronous agents independently of which runner it uses.
47	
48	With visitor execution, `concurrency` bounds invoked callbacks, including adapters and visitors. It does not bound externally dispatched agents after external deferral, enforce a token budget, or provide distributed claims. A returned/awaited callback must represent completion of its work: launching a background job and returning immediately releases its dependents too early.
49	
50	A host-controlled tick follows this sequence:
51	
52	```text
53	load graph revision + accepted facts
54	              ↓
55	materialize source → prepare reusable definition → create session → advance
56	              ↓
57	read frontier tickets → filter claims/waits → rank candidates → claim and dispatch agents
58	              ↓
59	validate result + attempt/revision → durably accept completion
60	              ↓
61	complete retained ticket + advance again, or reconstruct next tick
62	```
63	
64	The same vertex can remain in `readyOrDeferredIds` while an external agent is running. CTT's `activeVisitorVertexIds` tracks its own visitor chains, not the host's external attempts. Always overlay host claims, capacity, and waits before dispatch.
65	
66	## Discover the graph
67	
68	CTT traverses the graph your adapter provides; it does not generate a plan from a goal or work-item type. A host's `planDag` can select a type-specific template or generate and validate a revision, then adapt its nodes to CTT. `planDag` is a host function, not a CTT API. Hints describe how to discover that plan.
69	
70	| Concept                          | CTT representation                                                 | Host responsibility                                                |
71	| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
72	| Stable work identity             | `vertexId`                                                         | Choose IDs that can be reconstructed and matched to accepted facts |
73	| Opaque task data                 | `vertexContent.$data`                                              | Agent role, prompt/artifact references, policy and metadata        |
74	| Discovery and structure          | `resolveRoot()`, `resolveChild(hint)`, `vertexContent.$childHints` | Supply the complete intended catalog and structural relationships  |
75	| Initial-work dependency          | `dependsOnWork`                                                    | Declare which work must be accepted first                          |
76	| Structural-completion dependency | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`                                      | Declare which composite must finish before work begins             |
77	| Missing prerequisite lookup      | Optional `resolvePrerequisite(id)`                                 | Fetch graph facts from a catalog/service                           |
78	
79	For a known catalog, use `materializeDagInputFromRecords(items, { id, children?, dependsOnWork?, dependsOnSubgraphCompletion? })`. Every catalog item is discovered, including disconnected entries; `children` returns structural child IDs. A child ID absent from the catalog rejects immediately, while missing prerequisite IDs reach dependency validation. For nested records, `materializeDagInputFromRoots(roots, selectors)` expands `children(item)` records iteratively and shares repeated references. Different forest records with the same ID reject; `materializeDagInputFromRecords` rejects any duplicate ID. Async variants accept iterable/async-iterable inputs and value-or-promise selectors, then return the same input envelope containing a synchronous discovery source.
80	
81	Both adapters return `MaterializedDagInput` envelopes containing `traversableGraph` and `syntheticRoot: true`; pass or spread both fields together. `DagDiscoverySource` names the actual discovery protocol, while walking materializers return actual `GraphWalkSource` protocols. Both DAG adapters copy membership and edge lists once. Item data and IDs retain shallow identity: editing an item field remains visible, but editing its original edge array does not change captured topology. The hidden synthetic holder never appears in public vertices, callbacks, or events. For custom adapters, the equivalent catalog pattern uses `syntheticRoot: true`, lists every item in its `$childHints`, and declares explicit `dependsOnWork` lists. Discovery cannot detect work omitted from the supplied domain.
82	
83	Call `prepareDag(source)` or `await prepareDagAsync(source)` to discover and validate once. A valid result exposes `dag.liveVertexSummaries` and factories for independent runners or sessions; an invalid result exposes an `issues` array. Source errors retain their exact thrown values, including a source-thrown `DagTraversalStallError`. Structural child cycles throw `DagDiscoveryCycleError` with an identity-preserving closed `vertexIds` witness; malformed-source errors also throw. Only engine dependency validation failures become `{ kind: 'invalid', issues: [{ kind: 'milestone', diagnostics }] }`, using the same result shape as definition preparation, composition and revision.
84	
85	A prepared definition owns copied topology and detached readonly vertex descriptions. Each new session gets independent progress, accepted seeds, references, and settlement generations without calling the original adapter again. Replay hints are normalized to IDs; original opaque discovery hints are not retained. Preparation can perform source I/O, so business work belongs in host execution or visitors. See the [prepared definition contract](reference.md#reusable-prepared-dags).
86	
87	Discovery and execution dependencies are distinct. Graph sources default to `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'none'`: omitting `dependsOnWork` means no work prerequisites. Declare explicit lists (including `[]`), or set `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'discoveryParentWork'` to inherit the discovery parent's W when the list is omitted. Ordinary roots honor W by default; `rootWorkDependencies: 'ignore'` suppresses root W only, never C. Children of a synthetic root have no implicit dependency on the holder. See [discovery versus execution](reference.md#discovery-and-execution-as-separate-phases).
88	
89	A prerequisite ID alone does not make a vertex discoverable. Include it through hints/catalog entries or supply `resolvePrerequisite`. That hook may find further prerequisites transitively; concurrent demand is coalesced. Return `{ kind: 'found', vertex: { vertexId, vertexContent: { $data, $childHints }, dependsOnWork } }` for content, `{ kind: 'missing' }` for not found, or `{ kind: 'omitted', identity: null, satisfiesDependencies: true }` for intentional omission. Omission deliberately omits the vertex and satisfies its dependencies, so it is not a representation of a failed agent or a temporary service outage. Let adapter errors propagate as appropriate. See [lookup and identity rules](reference.md#discovery-and-completed-work).
90	
91	Choose discovery and dispatch surfaces by the lifetime you need:
92	
93	| Need                                             | Surface                                                                                      | Execution boundary                                                                                                                            |
94	| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
95	| Reuse validated topology across independent runs | `prepareDag(source)` / `prepareDagAsync(source)`                                             | Discover and validate once; create fresh runners or sessions afterward.                                                                       |
96	| Preview one fresh runner before work             | `runner.prepare()` / `await runner.prepare()`                                                | Discover and validate without visitors or dispatch generations; `run()` adopts that discovery.                                                |
97	| Discover fully, then execute in one operation    | Runner with `discovery: 'eager'`, then `run()`                                               | Validation precedes callbacks, but execution begins in the same call.                                                                         |
98	| Dispatch host work                               | Session `advance()` frontier tickets, or runner `summary().awaitingSettlement` after `run()` | Use external settlement; apply host claims and capacity. `readyOrDeferredIds` is observational dependency eligibility, not a dispatch ticket. |
99	
100	For a preview before dispatch, call `runner.prepare()` (await it on `AsyncDagTraversal`). It eagerly discovers the closure exposed by roots, hints and prerequisite lookup and validates the combined W/C graph, without visitors, execution events, new real-vertex completion, or deferred generations. Accepted `completedWork` seeds remain W facts. Inspect the graph at `HALTED` / `prepared`, then call `run()` to admit work without replaying discovery. Repeated preparation before execution is idempotent. This requires a fresh tree-source or graph-source runner without injected state/containers, even empty injected objects; invalid preparation requests reject recoverably. Once preparation begins, summaries report effective eager mode and eager topology freezing applies. After execution starts, preparation rejects.
101	
102	Preparation can perform adapter I/O: keep business execution in the host or visitors. During async preparation, `requestPause()` stops future admissions but waits for admitted discovery callbacks to settle; callbacks are not canceled. The operation acknowledges `paused`; another `prepare()` continues it, or `run()` adopts discovery and executes. Failed preparation preserves the exact error. Empty and omitted-root previews still stop `prepared`.
103	
104	Lazy execution remains available without preparation and may expose partially discovered views and summaries. `summary()` is observational and never fetches vertices. Use `DagTraversal<Workflow, Workflow, TaskId>` and `DagDiscoverySource<Workflow, Workflow, TaskId>` to carry host IDs through sources, summaries and settlement independently of data/hints. Every typed live result supplies an own `vertexId`; materialize class getters as own fields. See [identity migration](migration-uniform-api.md#caller-specified-graph-identity-types).
105	
106	## Work dependencies and completion joins
107	
108	| Declaration                                       | Releases the dependent after…                                                                   | Example                                                      |
109	| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
110	| `dependsOnWork: ['research']`                     | Research's initial work completes (W)                                                           | Implementation can start from accepted research              |
111	| `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion: ['implementation']` | Implementation's committed completion transition (C), including discovery and retained children | Review waits for implementation and all its component tasks  |
112	| Both lists                                        | Every declared W and C prerequisite is satisfied                                                | Review waits for a composite and a separate test-plan result |
113	
114	Use work dependencies for flat agent tasks. Use completion dependencies when structural children are meaningful parts of a composite. Seeds in `completedWork` satisfy W only; children and completion visitors still have to complete before C is released.
115	
116	Avoid making a child wait on its own ancestor's C when that ancestor must wait for the child to complete. CTT validates combined milestone cycles; seeding W does not make an invalid graph valid. Completion prerequisites add C gates independently of the declared W lists and the optional parent-inheritance policy. The [completion example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-completion-dependencies-example.ts) demonstrates a valid sibling join.
117	
118	## Accept results and resume
119	
120	Event streams filter at delivery across tree, DAG and walking runners. A new iterator lease applies its `emitEvents` selection to buffered observations and deferred settlement events. Selection never replays work or callbacks; `visitorPhases` retains independent admission snapshots. For example, resume with `emitEvents: ['subgraphCompleted']` to consume completion observations while suppressing pending work observations. See the [delivery example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/event-delivery-selection-example.ts).
121	
122	Start from the [quickstart](../README.md#quickstart-find-the-next-agent-tasks). To advance its session after the host accepts `testPlan`, dispatch from the `advance()` frontier. This continuation assumes the quickstart's `session` and `accepted` values:
123	
124	```ts
125	const pending = session.advance();
126	if (pending.kind === 'awaitingSettlement') {
127	  const ticket = pending.workTickets.find(
128	    (work) => work.vertexId === 'testPlan',
129	  )!;
130	  // Retain the ticket before dispatch; validate revision/attempt on the result.
131	  accepted.add(ticket.vertexId); // In-memory simulation of durable acceptance.
132	  session.completeWork(ticket);
133	  const next = session.advance();
134	  if (next.kind === 'awaitingSettlement') {
135	    console.log(next.workTickets.map((work) => work.vertexId)); // ['review']
136	  }
137	}
138	```
139	
140	`advance()` drains execution and returns `awaitingSettlement` with readonly tickets, `paused`, or `finished`; async sessions return a promise. `completeWork(ticket)` and `failTraversal(ticket, error)` are synchronous. The first accepted report returns `{ kind: 'accepted' }`; the identical report returns `{ kind: 'alreadyAccepted' }`. A failure fails the whole runner and the next advance throws the exact error. Conflicting reports, copied/forged tickets, and tickets from another facade or session reject. Repeated observations of the same deferred work stay usable. Follow completion with advance to observe new work. Use `session.inspectMilestones().explain({ vertexId, milestone: 'work' })` to explain blockers without advancing, and `session.inspect()` for lifecycle state. `failTraversal` is the sole fatal settlement method.
141	
142	Tickets expose only `vertexId`; their provenance and generation are private. They are local capabilities: serializing or copying a ticket does not preserve settlement authority. Filter each frontier through host claims, waits, and capacity. A ticket is not a distributed lease or persistent attempt ID. Use `summary()` for work progress/frontier, `inspectMilestones()` for dependency blockers, and `inspect()` for execution/iterator state. All three observe without advancing. `requestPause()` delegates cooperative pause to the runner.
143	
144	For existing custom-source runners, set `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'` and wrap with `bindDagWorkSession(runner)` or `bindAsyncDagWorkSession(runner)`. Wrapping runs no callbacks and acquires no separate execution owner; direct runner access remains available. The lower-level guarded frontier and settlement contract also remains available.
145	
146	For an async runner, await `runner.run()`. `settle()` itself is synchronous. A settlement wakes an active async consumer; after idle settlement, resume explicitly. Only one iterator may own a runner at a time. All runners expose `requestPause(): boolean`: true records a new request only while RUNNING, rather than acknowledging a halt. The active owner drains admitted chains to `HALTED` / `paused` without cancellation; a suspended iterator may need `next()` or `return()` to drive that boundary. Resume the same runner without replaying committed work.
147	
148	Dispatch from `summary().awaitingSettlement`: each readonly record atomically contains `{ vertexId, generation }`. It includes exactly live deferred work without an accepted outcome, in discovery order; queued-only, completed and deleted vertices are absent. Arrays and records are detached, retaining opaque ID identity. Filter this snapshot through host claims and capacity. DAG event `kind: 'workCompleted'` emits after committed W, including settlement; `kind: 'subgraphCompleted'` emits after committed C. Select these kinds with `emitEvents`; select readiness callbacks separately with `visitorPhases`. Committed events have no callback `phase` field. Seeded work emits no synthetic work event. `ON_WORK_READY` visitors remain pre-work. Completion events are not dispatch signals. Alternatively, an actual enabled `ON_WORK_READY` callback can dispatch before the external policy defers its chain. All callback commands commit before normal external deferral. `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` remains automatic once W, discovery, children, and C prerequisites permit it.
149	
150	Capture the generation belonging to the deferred work you dispatched. It is a local guard, not a durable attempt ID, distributed lease, or authentication token. The host must separately reject stale revisions, stale attempts, duplicate result delivery, and lost claims before accepting a result. An identical accepted settlement returns `false`; invalid, conflicting, or cross-runner settlement throws.
151	
152	`{ kind: 'workCompleted' }` means the work is complete for dependency traversal. An accepted review rejection can still complete a review vertex if host policy says the review work is done. `{ kind: 'traversalFailed', error }` fails the whole runner and preserves the exact thrown value; it is not a retry request or a business outcome field. The progress state `completed` means traversal work completion.
153	
154	## Persist facts and reconstruct
155	
156	CTT does not prescribe a storage engine or ship a persistence adapter. Define storage interfaces in your host and implement them with SQLite, PostgreSQL, a service, or another provider. Provider interchangeability must preserve the host's claim and result-acceptance guarantees, not just CRUD method names.
157	
158	| Persist in the host                                                          | Purpose                                                                        |
159	| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
160	| Graph revision, stable IDs, task definitions, W/C declarations and structure | Reconstruct the intended graph and associate results with the correct revision |
161	| Accepted outcomes and artifact references                                    | Decide which work is complete for traversal and supply downstream inputs       |
162	| Attempts, claims/leases, wait state, retry decisions and deduplication keys  | Prevent readiness from dispatching duplicate or ineligible work                |
163	| Accepted completion facts for the revision                                   | Supply `completedWork` to a new runner                                         |
164	
165	Keep prepared definitions, runners, tickets, vertex references, generation symbols, pending promises, and lookup handles in memory. A serialized summary is useful for presentation, but is not a runner checkpoint. CTT allows arbitrary SameValueZero IDs; durable hosts should choose their own stable serializable ID convention, such as strings.
166	
167	On startup or each reconciliation tick:
168	
169	1. Load a consistent graph revision and its host-accepted facts.
170	2. Prepare the full graph revision (plus lookup if required); reuse its in-memory definition while that revision remains valid.
171	3. Create a fresh session with `completedWork` and call `advance()`.
172	4. Filter frontier tickets using persisted claims, waits, retries, and host capacity.
173	5. Claim and dispatch selected work. Validate incoming results and durably record accepted completion before completing a retained ticket.
174	
175	This ordering lets a crash after acceptance but before settlement recover by reconstruction. A crash during an external side effect still needs host idempotency, reconciliation, or compensation; CTT does not provide exactly-once external execution. Transactional claim/acceptance, compare-and-set revisions, and dispatch outboxes are host design choices, not built-in CTT guarantees.
176	
177	The [reconciliation example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-reconciliation-example.ts) verifies that reconstructing from accepted facts yields the same ready IDs as advancing a retained runner. It uses an in-memory set to illustrate the contract, not a durable storage implementation.
178	
179	## Retries, human waits, and graph revisions
180	
181	A revision returns invalid issues or a fresh `{ dag, changes }`; the original prepared value and its sessions remain usable. Removing a vertex leaves its references and descendants in place, so repair those references explicitly in the same batch. Data comparisons in `changes` are shallow and cannot determine whether a previously accepted artifact remains useful.
182	
183	Keep host revision/attempt checks when results arrive. A ticket issued before revision throws in the new session and can still settle its original work. An admitted old async callback continues in its original runner; revision does not cancel it. Supply `completedWork` explicitly to the new session only for facts independently accepted for its definition. See [validated revision contracts](reference.md#validated-dag-revisions) and the [executable revision example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-revision-example.ts).
184	
185	- **Agent retry:** retain the task as incomplete; record the failed attempt and retry policy in the host. Do not send fatal `kind: 'traversalFailed'` unless you intend to fail the runner. Deferral must be the only command in its result; mixed results are rejected before any commands apply.
186	- **Human input or approval:** keep the task deferred and record a host wait. Exclude it from dispatch until the response is accepted; readiness alone will keep listing it.
187	- **New plan or graph revision:** use `reviseDag(prepared, operations)` to validate an atomic batch of full declaration edits, then start a session from the valid result. Carry completion facts forward only when the host validates their meaning for the new revision. Do not seed every historic success blindly.
188	- **Cancellation or timeout:** cancel host executor work separately. Halting CTT does not cancel already-started callbacks or remote agents. Async close may wait for a pending callback.
189	- **Completion side effects:** prefer durable result acceptance in the host. Reconstruction can invoke completion visitors again even when initial work was seeded; make any external effects idempotent.
190	
191	## Troubleshoot a workflow
192	
193	| Symptom                                              | Check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
194	| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
195	| Work completed without an agent running              | Check `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'`; the default `afterWorkReadyChain` completes W on normal callback-chain return. Seeds also mark W complete                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
196	| The same agent task dispatches again                 | Host claim/attempt state must filter `readyOrDeferredIds`; deferral intentionally leaves work ready                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
197	| Ready work seems absent                              | Run discovery first; inspect discovery completeness, seed IDs, and unmet W/C dependencies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
198	| Missing prerequisite or cycle                        | Inspect the `milestone` issue in `invalid.issues` from source preparation or `DagTraversalStallError` from direct execution for W/C constraints. For engine-detected structural cycles, `prepareDag`/`prepareDagAsync` return `invalid` with a `discoveryCycle` issue containing the ordered closed witness; direct runners throw `DagDiscoveryCycleError`. Collection adapters reject absent child IDs with `TypeError`. Authored definitions report `invalid.issues`; exact source/caller-thrown values propagate unchanged. Check catalog coverage, lookup results and structural edges |
199	| A seeded composite still blocks review               | Seeds complete W, not C; its retained children and completion transition must finish                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
200	| A retry aborts everything                            | `settle(..., { kind: 'traversalFailed', error }, ...)` is fatal; keep retryable work incomplete in host policy                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
201	| Settlement fails after restart                       | Generations are runner-local; reconstruct from accepted facts rather than replaying an old handle                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
202	| An external task still runs after halt               | Callback/executor cancellation belongs to the host                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
203	| A node fetched by lookup is missing from a root walk | Resolved prerequisites may be detached; enumerate `getVertexRefs()` instead of only walking `getRoot()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
204	
205	Use synchronous `runner.inspectMilestones()` (also on async runners), or the equivalent `inspectDagMilestones(runner)`, when a host needs to show why a milestone is blocked or which original constraints depend on it. Capture once, then call `explain({ vertexId, milestone: 'work' | 'subgraphCompletion' })`, `prerequisitesOf(...)`, or `dependentsOf(..., { transitive: true })`. Explanations distinguish `unresolved`/`deleted` identities, `omitted` vertices, unfinished work, incomplete local discovery and pending completion transitions. A ready or externally deferred task still has unfinished W; a seeded parent's W may be satisfied while its C waits for children. Constraint endpoints include work state and milestone satisfaction, without interpreting business outcomes.
206	
207	Inspect after `prepare()` for an eager validated view, or during lazy traversal for partial facts. `discoveryComplete: false` limits the captured domain, and an unresolved endpoint is not a proven missing task. Captures stay unchanged after settlement; capture again to refresh. These queries perform no callbacks, lookup, scheduling, or ownership changes, including while an iterator or pending async callback owns the runner. Static navigation keeps original constraints after milestones complete; explanations stop at satisfied milestones. See the [query contract](reference.md#dag-dependency-queries-and-explanations) and [runnable inspection example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-inspection-example.ts).
208	
209	Use `summary()` for DAG work readiness and diagnostics. Use `inspect()` for callback/iterator execution state. Inspection reports callback `phase` separately from chain `state`, `visitorIndex`, and admitted `executionOptions`; pending requests name their public callback `operation`. Graph `visitStage` records scheduling boundaries and cannot establish active callbacks or host-agent progress; deferred work may remain `INITIAL_VISIT_STARTED` after callbacks drain. Both are observational; neither drives traversal. See [progress contracts](reference.md#deferred-dag-progress-and-reconciliation) and [inspection](reference.md#inspection-and-execution) for exact fields and limits.
210	
211	### Carrying completion facts into a revision
212	
213	Unknown `completedWork` IDs reject intentionally. Before seeding a revised definition, the host must revalidate which accepted artifacts still satisfy its task policy, then retain only IDs present in `dag.liveVertexSummaries` or `dag.definition.omittedIds`. Membership alone does not establish that an old result is valid for changed task data or dependencies. Keep accepted facts outside CTT; revision does not migrate them automatically. See the [revision example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-revision-example.ts).
214	
215	### Observing traversal state
216	
217	Use `getResolvedTreeView()` or `getResolvedGraphView()` for live queries.
218	Callbacks and sources receive `resolvedTreeView` or `resolvedGraphView` and
219	canonical `VertexHandle` / `VertexView` facets. They cannot replace CTT state or
220	edit its hint collections; use visitor commands for active rewrites and deletion.
221	Caller data, IDs, and individual hints retain shallow identity. Captured event
222	vertices remain historical even when their live handles change. Synthetic DAG
223	entry source contexts have null parent vertex/ref fields; ordinary graph and tree
224	parents remain visible. See [query contracts](reference.md#safe-tree-queries).
225
