35	## General graph walking
36	
37	The `GraphWalk` / `AsyncGraphWalk` family explores shared, cyclic information graphs independently of DAG work scheduling. Import from the package root, the `graphWalk` namespace, or `configurable-tree-traversal/traversals/graph-walk`; constructors, helpers, commands and types share CJS/ESM identity. `walkGraph({ source, ...options })` and `await walkGraphAsync({ source, ...options })` run once and return the runner, including a resumable runner when a visitor halts. These helpers accept one canonical options object. For incremental iteration, start with `new GraphWalk({ source }).createRunner()`.
38	
39	Defaults are `strategy: 'breadthFirst'`, `revisit: 'once'`, vertex-only emission, all registered visitor phases enabled, and serial callbacks. Async walking permits value-or-promise callbacks and iterable/async-iterable sources; sync sources also feed async walkers. There is no concurrency option: supplying an own `concurrency` field rejects on either family. Sync types reject async sources, predicates and visitors; runtime also rejects thenables. No walking relationship means W/C readiness or settlement.
40	
41	<!-- standalone -->
42	
43	```ts
44	import {
45	  GraphWalk,
46	  GraphWalkPhase,
47	  materializeWalkSourceFromRecords,
48	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
49	
50	const source = materializeWalkSourceFromRecords(
51	  [
52	    { id: 'note', links: ['symbol', 'symbol'] },
53	    { id: 'symbol', links: ['note'] },
54	  ],
55	  {
56	    id: (item) => item.id,
57	    outgoing: (item) =>
58	      item.links.map((to) => ({ to, data: { kind: 'references' } })),
59	    roots: ['note'],
60	  },
61	);
62	const runner = new GraphWalk({ source }).createRunner();
63	for (const event of runner.iterateEvents({
64	  emitEvents: [GraphWalkPhase.EDGE],
65	})) {
66	  console.log(
67	    event.fromVertex.data.id,
68	    event.edge.outgoingIndex,
69	    event.edge.to,
70	    event.target.kind,
71	  );
72	}
73	console.log(runner.summary().outcome); // { kind: 'exhausted' }
74	```
75	
76	### Walking sources and identity
77	
78	`GraphWalkSource<Data, Edge, ID>` declares `hydration` alongside `roots()` and `outgoing(vertex)`. A vertex is `{ vertexId: ID, data: Data }`; a lazy link is `{ target, data: Edge }`. Choose one source mode:
79	
80	- `hydration: 'resolver'` requires `resolveVertex(id)`. Its roots and link targets can mix `{ vertexId }` with `{ vertexId, resolution }`.
81	- `hydration: 'inlineOrCached'` accepts no resolver: `resolveVertex` must be absent or yield `undefined` (including a captured getter). Any defined value rejects. Its roots and link targets are `{ kind: 'inline', vertexId, resolution }` or `{ kind: 'cached', vertexId }`. A cached target must already have an admitted resolution in this runner; first-use cache misses throw `TypeError` at admission. Inline roots therefore support cached self/backedges without a resolver.
82	
83	Resolution is `{ kind: 'found', data }` or `{ kind: 'omitted' }`. The `AsyncGraphWalkSource` counterpart preserves these modes and accepts promises and async iterables from source callbacks. Inline resolutions are already resolved tagged values; await hydration inside async callbacks/enumerators. Even object IDs use an explicit target wrapper to avoid confusing ID fields with resolution metadata.
84	
85	Source calls begin only during execution, not construction, configuration, runner creation or inspection. Each runner owns independent caches and source mode/callback/receiver snapshots. `roots()` must create independent iteration; roots and each adjacency enumeration must be finite. BFS consumes roots before descent; laziness does not guarantee fairness for infinitely branching sources. Empty/multiple roots need no synthetic holder. Repeated root declarations are deduplicated in declaration order under every policy.
86	
87	For each admitted target, consult the per-ID cache, then inline resolution, then `resolveVertex`. The **first accepted result is authoritative, including omission**. Later inline results for that ID are neither revalidated nor substituted. A pulled but rejected link cannot seed resolution: inline result contents are inspected only on eligible admission with a cache miss. Unlike DAG omission, a walking omission asserts no milestone satisfaction. Start a fresh walker to refresh an ID after omission or content replacement. Requested ID is authoritative; results cannot remap it. `found` accepts `null`/`undefined` data; unknown IDs are host errors unless deliberately omitted. A cached target cannot populate its own cache entry. No `missing` result exists.
88	
89	`resolveVertex` runs at most once per ID, and zero times when inline hydration wins. `outgoing` runs at most once per expanded found ID; adjacency is pulled incrementally and cached for other route occurrences. Pause retains partial enumeration; route replay uses cached links without repeating source I/O. Topology wrappers and traversal records are copied; caller data and IDs retain identity and are never frozen. A destination and optional inline-result reference are captured when its link is pulled. This is an observation over time, not a transactional snapshot of a changing host source.
90	
91	IDs use SameValueZero, including object/symbol identity and valid `undefined`, `null`, `NaN` and zero IDs. An edge is `{ from, outgoingIndex, to, data }`; its runner-local identity is source ID plus zero-based outgoing enumeration `outgoingIndex` **before filtering**; `from` and `to` express the ordinary walking direction. DAG child edge data retains its authored `slotIndex` independently of the outgoing enumeration coordinate. Parallel endpoint pairs, even repeated input wrappers, remain distinct. Compare identity fields rather than wrapper reference. Put a durable host relationship ID in edge data if needed; enumeration indices are not stable across runs.
92	
93	`materializeWalkSourceFromRecords(items, selectors)` consumes reusable `GraphWalkRecordSelectors<Data, Edge, ID>`; its async counterpart consumes `AsyncGraphWalkRecordSelectors`. Both selectors return `GraphWalkCatalogLink<Edge, ID>` records with readonly `to` and `data` fields. Catalog endpoint relations differ from lazy links with target wrappers. All walking materializers, including the DAG definition adapter, return synchronous sources declared as `hydration: 'resolver'`. Async eager materialization awaits the catalog once and returns that same reusable synchronous protocol.
94	
95	### Walking records and ordering
96	
97	Use `emitEvents: ['vertex', 'edge', 'path']` to select walking event kinds. Equivalent `GraphWalkPhase` enum values are also accepted for emission; `visitorPhases` uses `GraphWalkPhase.VERTEX`, `.EDGE`, and `.PATH`. Each phase invokes callbacks for its corresponding event kind:
98	
99	| Kind     | Fields                                                                                                                             |
100	| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
101	| `vertex` | `vertex`, route `depth`, incoming `via` edge or `null` for a root                                                                  |
102	| `edge`   | `edge`, found `fromVertex`, `depth` of the target route (source depth + 1), `target: { kind: 'found', vertex } \| { kind: 'omitted' }` |
103	| `path`   | Ordered `vertices`, ordered `edges`, route `depth`                                                                                 |
104	
105	In an edge record, `fromVertex` is the found source vertex; the constructor’s `source` is the adapter. Its `depth` describes the candidate target route even when that target is omitted. `GraphWalkEvent<Data, Edge, ID>` is that union. `GraphWalkEventFor<Data, Edge, Phase, ID>` and `GraphWalkPathEvent<Data, Edge, ID>` select precise records. Endpoint data stays typed; narrow `event.fromVertex.data.kind` and, after `event.target.kind === 'found'`, `event.target.vertex.data.kind` directly. No ID registry or fabricated tree `Vertex` is required. See the [typed reference example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-references-example.ts).
106	
107	A found root observes vertex then path. A followed link resolves/reuses its target, observes edge first, then vertex and path if a found occurrence is newly admitted under the policy. An omitted target of a followed link produces edge only. An omitted root has no incoming edge and produces no observation; it increments the `uniqueOmittedVertices` count and consumes a candidate read attempt and an admitted target. Record resolver outcomes in the host if omitted root IDs are needed. Under `once`, returning/self/parallel links still observe edges without repeated vertex/path observations. Visitor chains commit before their selected record emits. Expansion follows the occurrence's observations: a pause after yielding a vertex does not eagerly fetch adjacency. BFS preserves root/level source order; DFS exhausts each root's descendants before requesting the next root and follows outgoing order. Both are iterative. Pausing between edge and vertex retains pending observations and expansion without replaying resolution, completed callbacks or delivered records.
108	
109	`emitEvents` selects delivery; `visitorPhases` selects callbacks independently. Both use canonical field-wise selector patches, including empty selections and include/exclude filters; retired aliases reject. Hiding records/disabling callbacks changes neither discovery, budgets, nor revisit policy. An explicit call-level `emitEvents: [GraphWalkPhase.EDGE]` narrows every yield to edge records, including buffered records from an earlier lease. An omitted selector returns the broad union because persisted selectors can differ from defaults. Close the previous iterator before changing lease options. An admitted chain retains its callback configuration, while delivery uses the new lease's emission selection. Suppressed/delivered observations never replay; only pending observations before their delivery boundary can be newly selected. Tree and DAG iterators use the same delivery-time selection rule.
110	
111	Walking pending-request diagnostics use `operation: 'visit'` for callbacks in every walking phase. Source and iterator operations retain their distinct names, including `rootNext`, `edgeNext` and `iteratorReturn`.
112	
113	### Revisit policies, predicates, and bounds
114	
115	| `revisit`        | Vertex/path occurrences                              | Followed edges                                                      |
116	| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
117	| `once` (default) | One per found ID; path is its first-discovery prefix | Every followed link once, including back/self/parallel links        |
118	| `simplePaths`    | Each prefix without a repeated ID                    | Excludes a link closing a repeated vertex before `shouldFollowEdge` |
119	| `walks`          | Each prefix, including repeated IDs                  | Every eligible occurrence within bounds                             |
120	
121	Paths include zero-edge roots and every admitted prefix, not only leaves. Parallel links distinguish routes with identical vertex sequences. In route modes, a root reached from another root still contributes its own root path when declared; duplicate declarations of the same root do not. Source results/adjacency remain cached even when occurrences repeat. Use `once` for collecting reachable vertices and relationships; route enumeration can grow exponentially.
122	
123	`strategy: 'breadthFirst' | 'depthFirst'` chooses scheduling independently of revisit/emission. Depth counts route edges from zero. Under DFS/`once`, the first route fixes depth: finding a later shorter route does not re-expand a vertex. Use BFS for shortest discovery depth; DFS depth limits are not radius queries.
124	
125	`shouldFollowEdge(edge, context)` runs before target lookup; false prevents lookup through that occurrence. Context has found `fromVertex`, candidate target `depth`, and `revisit`; route policies add the current source-prefix `path`. The edge already identifies the relationship; context has no required `via`. `shouldExpandVertex(vertex, context)` runs after observations and before adjacency enumeration; context has occurrence `depth`, incoming `via`, `revisit`, and route `path` where applicable. False preserves observations while pruning expansion. Under `once`, the first expansion decision stands; route modes evaluate policy per prefix. The callback types are `GraphWalkEdgePredicate` and `GraphWalkExpansionPredicate`, with `Async` counterparts. Predicates must return booleans (promises allowed only for async). Commands do not control pruning.
126	
127	Limits are nonnegative safe integers, including zero. `simplePaths`/`walks` require `maxDepth` or `maxCandidateReadAttempts` at construction; `maxAdmittedTargets` alone is insufficient. Configuration patches validate merged options atomically and reject invalid transitions without mutation. A supplied `configure({ replaceLimits: ... })` record replaces the previous limits record; include each bound you want to retain. Runners snapshot options, selector arrays, visitor records and source callbacks/receiver; limits/topology policies are fixed for that runner. Larger bounds require a fresh runner. Unknown own option keys and unknown own limit keys reject with `TypeError` at construction or `configure()`, before discovery; invalid patches leave the previous configuration intact. Tree/DAG builders and public helper/option bags use the same strict own-key rule.
128	
129	| Limit                      | Accounting and boundary                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
130	| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
131	| `maxDepth`                 | Gate expansion at the occurrence boundary after `shouldExpandVertex`. Do not open outgoing at the boundary. A rejected expansion predicate contributes no depth cutoff. Otherwise conservatively report a cutoff even for an unqueried leaf. A returning edge under `once` alone does not trigger a cutoff. |
132	| `maxAdmittedTargets`       | One candidate for each distinct root and eligible followed link, including omissions and returning/parallel links. Edge+vertex+path still count as one. Check allowance before another pull; zero performs no source calls.                                                                                 |
133	| `maxCandidateReadAttempts` | One attempted root/link `next()`, including end-of-stream, duplicates, filtered/cycle-closing candidates and cached replay. No next pull after exhaustion; zero performs no source calls. Does not bound time inside host callbacks.                                                                        |
134	
135	Global limits drain the final admitted candidate's finite observation chain (unless paused), then finish. Depth pruning permits other branches to continue. At an exact cap, do not pull extra data merely to prove exhaustion; report exhausted only if the final allowed pull already proves all work drained. Otherwise report limited. Limits do not cancel callbacks.
136	
137	`summary()` returns detached `{ status, counts, outcome }`. Counts are `candidateReadAttempts`, `admittedTargets`, unique cached `uniqueFoundVertices`/`uniqueOmittedVertices`, `discoveredLinks` (distinct source links pulled before filtering, without counting cached route replay again), and processed `processedObservations: { vertex, edge, path }` independently of filters. Each phase counter advances at its observation acknowledgement, including suppressed records and disabled callbacks. `outcome` is `null` before terminal completion; `{ kind: 'exhausted' }`; `{ kind: 'limited', reasons }`; `{ kind: 'closed' }`; or `{ kind: 'failed', error }`. Reasons are unique and ordered `maxDepth`, `maxAdmittedTargets`, `maxCandidateReadAttempts`. Exhaustion means the configured source/policy drained, not completeness of a remote graph. Reaching `maxAdmittedTargets` reports `limited` even if the last admitted occurrence happened to be the final one: checking the next iterator result would violate the no-speculative-pull bound. To prove exhaustion, leave allowance beyond the expected admissions (distinct roots plus eligible followed links, not just distinct vertices). Always report outcome when presenting bounded provenance; see the [path example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-paths-example.ts).
138	
139	### Walking visitors, pause, close, and errors
140	
141	Use phase-keyed constructor visitors or `addVisitorFor`, `addVisitorGroupFor`, `setVisitorsFor`, `listVisitorsFor`. Flat registrations sort by priority before batching; explicit ordered groups retain group order/batching. Query wrappers are detached with shared callbacks/group metadata. Context supplies exact `phase`, zero-based `admissionIndex`, phase-local logical `phaseObservationIndex`, `visitorIndex`, and readonly descriptive `registration`. Callbacks receive walking event records, not tree vertices. Only existing `TraversalVisitorCommandName.PAUSE_TRAVERSAL` and `NOOP` commands are accepted, with absent or explicitly `undefined` `commandArguments`; non-undefined arguments reject. Settlement, mutation, subtree, deletion and chain-state commands reject. `commandCommitMode` controls `afterGroup` / `afterEachVisitor` boundaries independently of serial async execution. `PAUSE_TRAVERSAL` retains callback progress and resumes without replay.
142	
143	`run()` returns `this` synchronously or `Promise<this>` asynchronously; `iterateEvents()` returns a closeable generator/async generator. One execution owner is allowed. Competing/reentrant execution rejects without poisoning the owner; async calls on the owning iterator queue in order. Closing a never-started consumer iterator performs no source I/O. Active iterator `return()`, loop `break` or consumer-body error releases ownership and pauses while retaining caches/source iterators. `requestPause()` records a request only while RUNNING; the owner drains admitted callback work to a safe boundary. `isHalted()` and `getStopReason()` expose pause; walking has no awaiting-settlement state. Source/predicate/visitor failures retain exact thrown values, including `null` and `undefined`; subsequent execution rethrows that value. FINISHED runners never restart.
144	
145	Runner `close()` is terminal resource disposal, distinct from consumer iterator `return()`. Exhaustion, limits, explicit close, and failure dispose still-open source iterators by calling `return` in reverse acquisition order. Attempt all cleanup even when one fails; exhausted iterators need no return. An existing source/predicate/visitor failure wins over cleanup errors; otherwise the first cleanup failure wins and leaves FAILED. **Closing an already failed runner rethrows/rejects its exact retained error without repeating cleanup. Overlapping async closes share the same promise.** Repeated close is idempotent for state/resource effects. Successful close reports FINISHED/closed; closing an already successfully finished runner preserves its outcome.
146	
147	Terminal close requires no active execution owner; close during an active run/iterator rejects without changing its owner. First close the public iterator or request and await pause. Async iterator return immediately requests pause during an in-flight request, drains that admitted work, resolves pending next calls as done on successful return, and retains undelivered observations. A rejecting pending request remains the exact primary traversal failure. Consumer iterator throw retains its own consumer error for that throw call. Terminal close then prevents resumption and awaits resource cleanup without synthesizing further results. Neither pause nor close cancels promises or interrupts host work. Pending host work must eventually settle for pause acknowledgement/cleanup to finish. Consumer-body errors remain consumer errors and leave traversal resumable rather than becoming retained traversal failures. Use explicit terminal close when abandoning a paused runner, and handle its retained failure when applicable.
148	
149	### Walking adapters and inspection
150	
151	`materializeWalkSourceFromRecords(items, { id, outgoing, roots })` eagerly copies a finite catalog. `outgoing(item)` returns `{ to, data }` links; roots are explicit IDs. The adapter maps each catalog `{ to, data }` to a lazy-source `{ target: { vertexId: to }, data }` link and resolves targets from its validated catalog. Custom lazy sources use the target wrapper and may supply an inline `resolution`; catalog links use only `to` and `data`. Any extra inline hydration fields are ignored, and target data comes from the catalog. It rejects duplicate vertex IDs, unknown roots and unknown targets, preserves order/parallel links, and shares caller IDs/data. `await materializeWalkSourceFromRecordsAsync(...)` awaits finite inputs, roots and selectors once, then returns the same reusable **synchronous** source. These eager adapters differ from lazy custom source callbacks.
152	
153	`materializeWalkSourceFromDagDefinition(definition, { relations })` requires a nonempty duplicate-free selection of `children`, `workDependencies`, `subgraphCompletionDependencies`. Roots follow entry order. Links point parent-to-child or dependent-to-prerequisite, in canonical children/work/completion order and declaration order within each. `GraphWalkDagRelation` is `{ kind: 'child', slotIndex } | { kind: 'workDependency' } | { kind: 'subgraphCompletionDependency' }`; the former name `DagWalkRelation` is not an alias. Preserve parallel child slots; anonymous omissions produce no target, known omitted IDs resolve as omissions. This adapter performs shape normalization and selected-topology membership checks, permits cycles, invokes no source I/O, and does not prepare/validate execution dependencies or assert W/C facts.
154	
155	Declared live/omitted IDs must always be unique and disjoint. Selected child slots and roots-entry slots must agree with their declared live/omitted kind; root and selected W/C IDs may name either. Unselected child endpoint consistency is ignored after shape normalization, and unselected dependencies do not impose membership constraints. Selected unresolved endpoints reject. Owned topology and **adapter-generated relationship labels** are detached, including across outgoing calls/runners; ordinary caller-supplied edge data remains shared by identity. Walking sources are explicit adapters, not a common interface retrofitted onto `TreeSource` / `DagDiscoverySource`.
156	
157	`inspect(): GraphWalkInspection` is synchronous, detached, frozen and passive on both runner families. It exposes common execution fields plus `kind: 'graph-walk'`, `sourceMode: 'graph'`, `concurrency: 1`, strategy, revisit, effective `executionOptions`, counters, frontier size, open source iterator count, pending observation phases, active visitor phase/`visitorIndex`, and pending request IDs/operations with optional runner-local `vertexToken` symbols. Tokens are not caller IDs. No callbacks, data, promises or kernel closures leak into inspection. It neither advances sources nor acquires ownership. For common cross-family wrappers and detailed-type defaults, see [inspection and execution](#inspection-and-execution).
158	
159	## Configuration patches
160	
161	Builders configure future runners; an existing runner retains its configuration snapshot. Sync and async variants use the same rules.
162	
163	| Field                                            | Omitted or `undefined` patch                                     | Defined patch                                                                                  |
164	| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
165	| Walking `shouldFollowEdge`, `shouldExpandVertex` | Retain the previous predicate                                    | Callback replaces it; `null` clears it. Initial `null` also means absent.                      |
166	| Walking `replaceLimits`                          | Retain previous limits                                           | Replace the entire limits record; include every bound to retain.                               |
167	| `visitors` and `emitEvents` / `visitorPhases`    | Retain unspecified fields                                        | Patch visitor phases and selector fields independently, under their existing validation rules. |
168	| DAG `traversableTree` / `traversableGraph`       | Inherited keys and own `undefined` keys retain the active source | An own defined same-family source replaces it; an opposite-family source rejects.              |
169	
170	Every supported configure field accepts an explicit `undefined` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: missing and undefined fields retain prior values. This includes tree sources, concurrency, scheduling fields, each visitor phase, and each in-order field. `null` clears only explicitly nullable fields (walking predicates and `transformChildHints`). Walking constructors accept `limits`; configuration patches use `replaceLimits` to replace that record. A patch containing the former `limits` key rejects, including own `undefined`. Malformed defined fields reject atomically before registrations or configuration change; an existing runner keeps its snapshot. DAG construction requires exactly one own defined source and configure cannot change its source family. Source getters are captured once per request, without calling source callbacks.
171	
172	Public builders, helpers, mutation binders, execution options and nested option bags reject unsupported own string or symbol keys with `TypeError`, including non-enumerable keys and keys whose value is undefined. Source protocol objects can carry caller state and inherited methods; opaque data and IDs are not option bags. Path query options also reject unsupported own keys: `requirePathTo` / `requirePathsTo` accept only optional boolean `noRoot` and `noSelf` controls. Omitted or undefined controls use the default behavior, and accessors are captured once per query.
173	
174	## DAG traversal
175	
176	`DagTraversal` and `AsyncDagTraversal` traverse a discovered acyclic graph in two lifecycle orders: `ON_WORK_READY` visits eligible initial work, and `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` visits structural completion after the vertex’s work, discovery, and retained children complete. Under default `afterWorkReadyChain`, normal initial visitor-chain completion (including empty or filtered chains) satisfies work dependents; `externalSettlement` requires guarded host settlement; committed completion satisfies completion dependents. `dependsOnWork: [p]` waits for p's completed initial work (W); `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion: [p]` waits for p's committed `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` transition (C), including closed discovery and completion of every retained child. Both lists gate `ON_WORK_READY` conjunctively. Completion admission or an unfinished async completion callback does not satisfy C. Dependencies do not create structural parent/child edges; graph sources have no implicit parent W by default. Set `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'discoveryParentWork'` to inherit parent W when `dependsOnWork` is omitted; explicit lists, including `[]`, always win. Tree sources retain structural order and parent dependencies and reject explicit `rootWorkDependencies` or `dependsOnWorkDefault` options, including configuration patches. Graph source defaults are `rootWorkDependencies: 'honor'` and `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'none'`.
177	
178	<!-- standalone -->
179	
180	```ts
181	import {
182	  DagTraversal,
183	  DagVisitorPhase,
184	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal/traversals/dag-traversal';
185	import type { VertexTypes } from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
186	
187	type Workflow = VertexTypes<string, string>;
188	function runTask(task: string): void {
189	  console.log(`Running ${task}`);
190	}
191	const jobs: Record<string, { children: string[]; dependsOnWork: string[] }> = {
192	  root: { children: ['compile', 'test', 'publish'], dependsOnWork: [] },
193	  compile: { children: ['publish'], dependsOnWork: ['root'] },
194	  test: { children: ['publish'], dependsOnWork: ['root'] },
195	  publish: { children: [], dependsOnWork: ['compile', 'test'] },
196	};
197	const traversal = new DagTraversal<Workflow>({
198	  traversableGraph: {
199	    resolveRoot: () => makeJob('root'),
200	    resolveChild: (id) => makeJob(id),
201	    getVertexIdFromHint: (id) => ({ vertexId: id }),
202	  },
203	});
204	traversal.addVisitorFor(DagVisitorPhase.ON_WORK_READY, (vertex) => {
205	  runTask(vertex.getData());
206	});
207	traversal.createRunner().run();
208	
209	function makeJob(id: string) {
210	  const job = jobs[id];
211	  if (job === undefined) throw new Error(`Unknown job: ${id}`);
212	  return {
213	    kind: 'found' as const,
214	    vertex: {
215	      vertexId: id,
216	      dependsOnWork: job.dependsOnWork,
217	      vertexContent: { $data: id, $childHints: job.children },
218	    },
219	  };
220	}
221	```
222	
223	A DAG constructor accepts exactly one source mode. Use `traversableGraph` for graph callback options, explicit ids and dependencies; use `traversableTree` to adapt an existing tree source while visitors receive the graph facade. The source mode is fixed at construction, although `configure()` can replace the adapter within that mode. Tree-source results reject graph identity, `dependsOnWork`, and `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`, including fields explicitly set to undefined.
224	
225	Graph sources and DAG APIs accept a trailing identity type, for example `DagDiscoverySource<Workflow, Workflow, TaskId>` and `DagTraversal<Workflow, Workflow, TaskId>`. It flows through dependencies, prerequisite lookup, completed-work seeds, settlement, visitors, graph views/snapshots, summaries and diagnostics. Data, rewrite data, and child hints keep their existing generic positions. Constructors and helpers infer identity from typed graph sources; use an explicit union for heterogeneous identities when inference cannot combine them. `ResolvedGraphView<T, ID>`, `DagSummary<ID>`, `DagVertexProgress<ID>` and `DagTraversalStallDiagnostics<ID>` default to `unknown` for compatibility. Visitor types append ID after their phase parameter, for example `DagVisitor<T, R, DagVisitorPhase.ON_WORK_READY, ID>`.
226	
227	Selecting an ID domain other than `unknown` requires an explicit `vertexId` on every live graph-source result, including prerequisite results. Omitted results instead supply an explicit `identity` wrapper or `null`. Default `unknown` sources retain generated-ID fallback and prerequisite-ID inheritance. Tree-source DAG mode generates reference identities and therefore accepts only the default `unknown` ID domain. TypeScript cannot express property ownership, so graph result normalization rejects an inherited `vertexId` with `TypeError` before generated-ID or prerequisite-ID fallback. Class adapters must materialize an own field, for example `{ kind: 'found', vertex: { vertexId: instance.vertexId, vertexContent: instance.vertexContent } }`; an own getter is also supported. Legitimately absent IDs retain default-`unknown` fallback, and explicit own `vertexId: undefined` retains the real undefined identity. ID values are never coerced or schema-validated. Public graph views and milestone snapshots exclude synthetic-root bookkeeping and retain `ID`. Raw runner containers and their synthetic holder identities are private.
228	
229	Graph ids use `Map`/`Set` SameValueZero equality, so `NaN`, `null`, explicit `undefined`, symbols, and object references are valid. `getVertexIdFromHint()` returns a wrapper, not a bare id: return `{ vertexId: undefined }` for the real id `undefined`, or return `undefined` when the hint has no identity. A known hint id can reuse a vertex without resolving it; if both the hint hook and resolver supply ids, they must match.
230	
231	Stalled DAG runners throw `DagTraversalStallError<ID = unknown>` (available from the root, `core`, and DAG traversal exports). Explicit type arguments type constructed errors and diagnostic annotations; an arbitrary catch value narrowed with `instanceof DagTraversalStallError` still has unknown IDs. The runner's ID type is not inferred through exceptions. Its `diagnostics` contains detached arrays while retaining original ID identity:
232	
233	- `dependencies`: `{ vertexId, unmetPrerequisiteIds }` entries for vertices waiting on prerequisites.
234	- `unknownPrerequisiteIds`: unmet IDs absent from the discovered graph; lazy discovery may still hide those vertices in the source.
235	- `dependencyCycleComponents`: stable raw-ID projections of W/C milestone cycles, including structural completion waits. A child waiting for ancestor C is invalid; ordinary child waits for parent W remain valid.
236	- `dependencyBlockedIds`: vertices with unmet prerequisites outside those cycles, including direct missing-prerequisite dependents and downstream blocked work.
237	- `structurallyIncompleteIds`: unfinished vertices without unmet prerequisites, typically ancestors waiting for children.
238	
239	The familiar `DAG traversal stalled:` message safely labels arbitrary IDs without coercing user objects. These diagnostics describe the terminal discovered graph; they do not fetch prerequisites or change scheduling.
240	
241	`runner.getResolvedGraphView()` provides read-only vertex, visit-stage, parent, child, path, and ID queries. Query arrays are shallow snapshots: changing an array cannot edit topology, while contained references and user vertex data remain live. With `retainOriginalGraphStructure: true`, DAG runners expose runner and callback `originalGraphView`, a progressively discovered `OriginalGraphView` containing first-accepted content and discovery edges. Rewrites and deletions do not alter it, but user data is still shallowly shared.
242	
243	Known omitted discovery slots retain `identity: { vertexId }` in `ChildSlot<T, ID>`; `identity: null` distinguishes anonymous omission from a known `undefined` identity. These slots remain omitted rather than structural children. Prepared definitions preserve their discovery positions when replaying the source.
244	
245	### Collection and forest sources
246	
247	All four DAG input helpers return a `MaterializedDagInput<Item, ID>` envelope with `{ traversableGraph, syntheticRoot: true }` options for DAG constructors and preparation. Pass or spread the whole envelope into DAG options; nesting it under `traversableGraph` is invalid and extracting only the source loses synthetic-root treatment. Walking materializers retain their names because they return actual `GraphWalkSource` protocols. Their data is the caller's item and their hints are IDs (`VertexTypes<Item, ID>`).
248	
249	Materialized lookup does not depend on live vertex data: the source accepts any rewrite-data context R, with an input specialization retained for ordinary Item/ID inference on TypeScript 4.7/4.9. The same envelope therefore composes with an explicitly disjoint R in sync/async DAG builders and helpers without assertions or new factory arguments. Discovery results and original views remain Item, and hint replacement remains constrained to input ID hints. This built-in capability does not relax live-context checks for user sources with narrow hooks. See the [executable disjoint-rewrite example](migration-idiomatic-api.md#dag-inputs-and-actual-sources).
250	
251	| Helper                                                  | Input and selectors                                                                                                                            | Membership and identity                                                                                                                                                                              |
252	| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
253	| `materializeDagInputFromRecords(items, selectors)`      | Iterable items; required `id(item)`; optional `children(item)`, `dependsOnWork(item)`, `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion(item)` return iterable IDs | Every item is catalogued, including disconnected entries. Any duplicate ID rejects, even the same record twice. Structural child IDs must exist in the catalog; `children` returns IDs, not records. |
254	| `materializeDagInputFromRoots(roots, selectors)`        | Iterable root items; same selectors, but `children(item)` returns iterable items                                                               | Expands iteratively. `children` returns records, not IDs. The same record can appear under multiple parents; different records with the same ID reject.                                              |
255	| `materializeDagInputFromRecordsAsync(items, selectors)` | Iterable/async-iterable items; value-or-promise selectors, with iterable/async-iterable edge results                                           | Awaits materialization, then returns an input envelope containing a synchronous discovery source.                                                                                                    |
256	| `materializeDagInputFromRootsAsync(roots, selectors)`   | Iterable/async-iterable roots; value-or-promise selectors; children yield records                                                              | Awaits materialization, then returns the same input envelope with shared-root rules.                                                                                                                 |
257	
258	Absent edge selectors mean empty lists. All four adapters reject the retired selector keys `dependencies` and `completionDependencies` with `TypeError`, even when inherited or present with `undefined`, before reading the input or invoking selectors. Use `dependsOnWork` and `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion` so a stale selector cannot silently drop dependency edges. Caller task-data properties may still use any names, including `dependencies`. Structural child edges and work/completion dependency edges remain distinct. Missing prerequisite IDs are left to the existing validator. Structural discovery cycles become `discoveryCycle` issues in `prepareDag`/`prepareDagAsync`; direct runners throw `DagDiscoveryCycleError`. The synthetic holder is hidden from public vertices, events, callbacks, and parent queries.
259	
260	Materialization copies collection membership and edge arrays once. Later edits to caller arrays do not change topology; item data and opaque IDs remain shared shallow values and are never frozen. SameValueZero IDs, including `undefined`, `null`, `NaN`, symbols, and objects, retain their identity. Selector errors and async rejections propagate unchanged. See the [quickstart](../README.md#quickstart-find-the-next-agent-tasks) for a complete flat catalog.
261	
262	Dependency vocabulary describes the same two milestone relations across layers:
263	
264	| Layer                                            | Wait for work (W)   | Wait for completion (C)           |
265	| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
266	| Collection selectors                             | `dependsOnWork`     | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`     |
267	| Sources and definitions                          | `dependsOnWork`     | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`     |
268	| Milestone queries                                | `milestone: 'work'` | `milestone: 'subgraphCompletion'` |
269	| Walking relation selections and definition diffs | `workDependencies`  | `subgraphCompletionDependencies`  |
270	
271	Structural `children` remain a separate relation. Walking those declarations observes links; it does not execute or satisfy milestones.
272	
273	### Reusable prepared DAGs
274	
275	`prepareDag(input)` returns `PrepareDagResult<Data, ID>`; `prepareDagAsync(input)` returns a promise of the same union:
276	
277	- `{ kind: 'valid', dag: PreparedDag<Data, ID> }` contains a reusable validated definition.
278	- `{ kind: 'invalid', issues: readonly DagDefinitionIssue<ID>[] }` represents validation failure and provides no executable definition. Source dependency failures contain one `{ kind: 'milestone', diagnostics: DagTraversalStallDiagnostics<ID> }` issue. There is no top-level `diagnostics` alias.
279	
280	Inputs accept `traversableGraph`, `syntheticRoot`, `rootWorkDependencies`, and `dependsOnWorkDefault`; async preparation also accepts `concurrency`. Preparation eagerly discovers and validates without visitors or execution events. Visitors, completed-work seeds, injected continuation state, and source replacements belong outside this input. Source errors retain exact identity, even when the caller throws a `DagTraversalStallError`; malformed source contracts also throw rather than becoming invalid results.
281	
282	Engine-originated structural discovery cycles return an invalid preparation issue `{ kind: 'discoveryCycle', cycleWitnessVertexIds: readonly ID[] }`. The IDs retain the engine's ordered closed witness (first ID repeated at the end) and arbitrary caller identity; for `a -> b -> a` the discovered closing edge yields `['b', 'a', 'b']`. This witness differs from the unordered SCC membership in authored-definition `structuralCycle` issues. Direct runner execution and runner `prepare()` still throw `DagDiscoveryCycleError<ID = unknown>`, exported from the root, core and DAG subpaths, with the same readonly frozen `cycleWitnessVertexIds` witness. Structural SCC issues use `componentVertexIds`. Source-thrown values, including instances of that class or `DagTraversalStallError`, propagate unchanged across callback, getter and iterable reads. Collection adapters reject missing child IDs eagerly with `TypeError`, before preparation starts. Dependency invalidity appears in the `milestone` issue within `invalid.issues`.
283	
284	`dag.liveVertexSummaries` is a convenience projection of live vertices, not a round-trip source; its `children` omits omission slots. Use `dag.definition` for faithful reconstruction, composition and revision. The projection is a detached readonly array of descriptions: `{ vertexId, data, children, dependsOnWork, dependsOnSubgraphCompletion }`. Owned records and edge arrays are immutable, while data and IDs retain shallow caller identity. The definition preserves structural order, single-root versus multiple-entry semantics, omissions satisfying prerequisites, effective implicit dependencies, and the original root W policy. Replay normalizes discovery hints to ID links; original opaque hints and callback contexts are not captured.
285	
286	| Factory                                | Result                                                         | Options                                                                       |
287	| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
288	| `dag.createRunner(options?)`           | Prepared sync `DagTraversalRunner`                             | `visitors`, `completedWork`, `workCompletion`, `retainOriginalGraphStructure` |
289	| `dag.createAsyncRunner(options?)`      | Promise of a prepared async runner                             | Same options, plus `concurrency`                                              |
290	| `dag.createWorkSession(options?)`      | `DagWorkSession<ID>` using external settlement                 | `completedWork`                                                               |
291	| `dag.createAsyncWorkSession(options?)` | Promise of `AsyncDagWorkSession<ID>` using external settlement | `completedWork`, `concurrency`                                                |
292	
293	Each factory creates independent references, progress, visitors, seed copies, and settlement generations. New runners prepare replay topology before visitors execute and never call original source adapters. Replay may repeat in-memory validation. Runner data/hint types are `VertexTypes<Data, ID>`; event/visitor phase selection remains available through ordinary runner execution methods. The definition owns topology: attempts to replace sources, discovery/root/implicit-parent policies, sorting, or continuation state reject, including JavaScript own fields explicitly set to `undefined`. Session factories accept only the options listed above; use a custom configured runner plus coordination when visitors are needed.
294	
295	A prepared definition is an in-memory value, not a durable checkpoint or editable graph. Reconstruct from source facts after process loss and create a new definition for a new graph revision. The [foundations example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/agent-api-foundations-example.ts) verifies independent sessions and no original-source replay.
296	
297	#### Materialized DAG definitions
298	
299	`dag.definition` is a `DagDefinition<Data, ID>` containing ordered `vertices` (`vertexId`, `data`, `slots`, `dependsOnWork`, `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`), `omittedIds`, and an `entry` tagged as `root`, `roots`, or `empty`. Dependencies are the captured effective W/C constraints. A definition slot is `{ kind: 'vertex', vertexId }` or `{ kind: 'omitted', identity: { vertexId } | null }`; the wrapper preserves a known `undefined` identity separately from an anonymous omission. Resolved-graph `ChildSlot` uses the same explicit identity wrapper for this distinction. Anonymous omission slots in vertex records remain stored, while replay filters them without inventing ID hints. Root catalog slots require identities; repeated slots and shared children are allowed.
300	
301	`defineDag(input)` copies and freezes owned arrays and records, retaining shallow caller data and ID references. Malformed required fields and duplicate live/omitted identity declarations throw `TypeError`. SameValueZero identity applies throughout, including dependency deduplication. Shape normalization does not validate graph semantics.
302	
303	`prepareDagDefinition(definition)` normalizes and validates those source facts without callbacks or execution events. It returns `PrepareDagResult<Data, ID>`: `{ kind: 'valid', dag }` or `{ kind: 'invalid', issues }`. Invalid results have no executable DAG. Valid results retain authored declaration order, ordered slots, and entry mode, and support all prepared factories above. Programmer errors and exact accessor-thrown values propagate.
304	
305	| Issue kind                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                            |
306	| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
307	| `missingStructuralEndpoint` | A vertex slot targets a non-live ID; `parent: { vertexId }` identifies the owner, and `parent: null` denotes a roots entry slot.                                                                   |
308	| `invalidEntry`              | `reason` is `unknownRoot`, `anonymousCatalogEntry`, or `emptyWithVertices`; `vertexIds` names the offending root/live records, or is empty for an anonymous entry. Root entries require a live ID. |
309	| `invalidOmission`           | `vertexIds` lists identified omission slots absent from the declared omitted domain, including references to live IDs.                                                                             |
310	| `unreachable`               | `vertexIds` lists declared live or omitted identities outside the entry closure through structural slots and both W/C dependency lists. Detached prerequisites are valid.                          |
311	| `structuralCycle`           | `componentVertexIds` is structural SCC membership in declaration order, rather than an ordered cycle witness.                                                                                               |
312	| `milestone`                 | `diagnostics` contains the existing `DagTraversalStallDiagnostics<ID>` for unknown W/C endpoints or combined milestone cycles.                                                                     |
313	
314	Structural issues are deterministic and prevent replay; structurally valid definitions use the existing DAG milestone validator. Empty entries may retain known omitted IDs, including an omitted root, and those IDs remain recognized for completed-work seeds. An empty entry with live records is invalid. This API represents in-memory source topology; it carries no runner progress or automatic completion-fact migration.
315	
316	#### Definition diffs
317	
318	`diffDagDefinitions(before, after)` compares immutable `DagDefinition` values and returns a `DagDefinitionDiff<ID>` with frozen owned arrays and records. It performs no preparation, execution, serialization or deep traversal. The definitions may have different data types; IDs retain their caller identity.
319	
320	- `addedIds` follows new vertex order; `removedIds` follows old vertex order.
321	- `changedVertices` contains retained IDs in old vertex order, each with `aspects` in the fixed order `data`, `slots`, `workDependencies`, `subgraphCompletionDependencies`.
322	- `vertexOrderChanged` compares the full ordered live-ID sequence, so additions and removals also set it. Reordering alone does not add a changed vertex record.
323	- `entryChanged` compares entry mode and its ordered contents. `omissionsChanged` compares the ordered omitted-ID declarations.
324	
325	IDs use SameValueZero throughout, including slots and dependencies. Slot kind and omission identity wrappers remain significant: anonymous omission differs from known `undefined`. Slot, dependency and omission ordering changes count. Data uses `Object.is`: replacing a data object counts even if its fields are equal; same-reference deep mutation cannot be detected. The host decides whether artifacts and accepted completion facts remain valid; the diff does not infer business invalidation.
326	
327	### Validated DAG revisions
328	
329	`reviseDag<Data, ID>(prepared, operations)` returns `DagRevisionResult<Data, ID>`: `{ kind: 'valid', dag, changes }` or `{ kind: 'invalid', issues }`. Only a valid result exposes a fresh prepared DAG. The prepared value fixes the data/ID domain; operations cannot widen it. All revision functions and types are exported from the root, DAG subpath and `dagTraversal` namespace.

Start with the workflow guide for integration; use this page for exact lifecycle, identity, error, and compatibility contracts.

## On this page

- [General graph walking](#general-graph-walking)
